headline: BEANS SANK FRIDAY; SUMMIT WEEK OPENS WITH CROSSED SIGNALS
lead: Soybeans closed Friday at $13.03, down 16 cents on the week's last session as funds took profits ahead of the Trump-Xi summit set for Sep 24. Crude broke 5.6% the same day, its biggest single-session drop in weeks, while diesel stayed near record highs regardless.
teaser: Beans gave back 16 cents into the weekend; the summit that's supposed to fix that trades Wednesday.

one_number.context: Drovers reports placements hit a record low in August, the screwworm border closure and drought liquidation both still working through the pipeline.

action: Nothing to do at $13.03 beans over the weekend; a Monday close below $12.90 says the summit trade is unwinding, not building.

sections.title: BEANS PRICE THE SUMMIT, NOT THE CROP
sections.body:
- Soybeans closed Friday at **$13.03**, down 16 cents as fund liquidation and pre-weekend profit-taking hit ahead of the Sep 24 Trump-Xi meeting.
- ASA is publicly pushing Trump to make China address its soybean purchase commitments and the 10% retaliatory duty at that summit, not just show up.
sections.so_what: Beans are a headline trade this week, not a fundamentals trade.

sections.title: DIESEL STAYS TIGHT AS CRUDE BREAKS
sections.body:
- WTI crude closed Friday at **$95.47**, down 5.6%, its sharpest single-day drop in weeks, but AgWeb reports diesel prices are still sitting near records and squeezing farm margins.
- Macron is calling the G7 back to discuss another emergency oil release as Europe loses Saudi crude and diesel keeps climbing regardless of crude's pullback.
sections.so_what: Crude's drop didn't touch the diesel bill farmers are actually paying.

sections.title: CATTLE FIRM, FEEDER SUPPLY THE STORY
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed Friday at **$216.57**, up slightly, while feeders slipped to $333.55 as the market keeps digesting a record-low August placements print from Drovers.
- Tight feeder supply, the screwworm border closure, and drought-driven cow liquidation are all pointing the same direction: fewer cattle coming, not more.
sections.so_what: Record-low placements says the feeder shortage gets tighter before Aug 24 relief lands.

outside_the_pit.title: USDA opens 2026-27 ARC/PLC enrollment with 30M new base acres
outside_the_pit.body: USDA's revenue safety-net programs just got their first base acreage increase in two decades, meaning bigger coverage pools for the next crop year.

watch_list.desc: Trump-Xi summit; confirmed Chinese soybean tonnage above prior pace keeps $13 beans supported, silence sends them lower.
Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above last week's mark says no weather delay is building into yield.
Export Sales; beans under 1.5 MMT says the summit talk isn't converting to actual demand yet.

daily_quote.text: A good harvest answers many questions.

source_summary: AGSIST Daily desk synthesis of CME settlement data, USDA reports, and wire sources including AgWeb, Feedstuffs, Drovers, OilPrice.com, and The Fence Post.
